header.running_head: Rasulullaah ﷺ's Fervour for Salaah and the Extreme Importance he Gave to it

blocks.text: so long in (Tahajjud) salaah that his feet would swell.[^1]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) also reports that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah at night that his feet would swell. The rest of the narration is as quoted above.[^2]

Hadhrat Nu'maan bin Basheer (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah that his feet would cut (after becoming extremely chapped). The rest of the narration is as quoted above.[^3]

Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to stand so long in (Tahajjud) salaah at night that his feet would rupture. I said to him, 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Why do you do this when Allaah has forgiven all your past and future mistakes?' He replied, 'Should I then not be a grateful servant?'"[^4] The same has been reported from Hadhrat Mughiera (RA)[^5] and Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA)[^6]

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ used to exert himself so much in Ibaadah that he became like an old water bag. 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' the Sahabah (RA) said, 'What makes you do this? Has Allaah not forgiven all your past and future mistakes?' He replied, 'Of course! Should I then not be a grateful servant?'"[^7]

Hadhrat Humayd narrates that when Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) was once questioned about the salaah Rasulullaah ﷺ performed at night, he replied, "The times we wanted to see Rasulullaah ﷺ performing salaah at night, we would see him and the times we wanted to see him asleep, we also saw him (he would spend part of the night in salaah and also sleep). There were times when he fasted so often during the month that we would think he will now not stop fasting. Then there were also times when he would not fast for so long that we would think he would now not fast at all (that month)."[^8]

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) relates, "I followed Rasulullaah ﷺ in salaah one night and he remained standing so long that I contemplated doing something terrible." "What was it that you contemplated?" the people asked. Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) replied, "I actually contemplated sitting down and leaving."[^9]
Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) narrates that Rasulullaah ﷺ once stood the entire night until dawn (in salaah) reciting the verse:

blocks.arabic_text: اِنْ تُعَذِّبْهُمْ فَاِنَّهُمْ عِبَادُكَ ۚ وَاِنْ تَغْفِرْ لَهُمْ فَاِنَّكَ اَنْتَ الْعَزِيْزُ الْحَكِيْمُ

blocks.text: Bazzaar, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.2 Pg.271). Tabraani has reported a similar narration from Hadhrat Abu Juhayfah (RA).
